niche.habitat: Alpine slopes, Rock spire, Giant tree canopy, Sea arches

chains.trait: Patagial membrane stretching between limbs on leaps
links: Dense air (1.6 bar) creates high drag and low terminal velocity
Falls are survivable; gliding is energetically cheap
Membranes evolve to convert falls into forward travel
Gliding reduces energy cost of traversing steep terrain

skill.effect: Leaps from height and glides; covers distance without stamina cost; allows escape from ground chases.

chains.weakness: Ground movement is slow; gales and turbulence can ground it or blow it off course.
observe: Leaps from cliff, stretches skin between limbs, and glides silently.
Landing is soft and controlled; no heavy thud.
Creature perches on high spires and drops to food.

journal.en: It falls only when it chooses, riding the heavy air.

plausibility.summary: F4 matches textbook glider physics on Primigenia: higher drag lowers terminal velocity (~25% per canon), making parachuting/gliding safer and cheaper than on Earth; steep andesite terrain (F7, F9) rewards gap-crossing without powered flight. Sprint cost and short chases fit Merodeador ground slowness.
fixes: F4 matches textbook glider physics on Primigenia: higher drag lowers terminal velocity (~25% per canon), making parachuting/gliding safer and cheaper than on Earth; steep andesite terrain (F7, F9) rewards gap-crossing without powered flight. Sprint cost and short chases fit Merodeador ground slowness.

analogues.organism: Malayan colugo (Galeopterus variegatus) and sugar glider (Petaurus): interlimb patagium converts height into horizontal travel.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded
see the cited works; chain wording is the council's own

chains.trait: UV-reflective plumage shimmering blue-white in noon sun
links: High slopes have 1.4× UV radiation hazard
DNA damage risk selects for UV protection
Reflective pigments or structural coloration evolve to scatter UV
Bright appearance may also signal fitness or startle prey

skill.effect: Immune to UV damage on high slopes; reduces stamina drain in bright sun.

chains.weakness: Highly visible to predators in open; overheat risk if sheltered too long.
observe: Plumage reflects sunlight like a mirror in midday.
Creature active only in bright light; avoids shade.
No sunburn marks on skin or feathers.

journal.en: A mirror for the burning sky.

plausibility.summary: Call it patagial and dorsal keratinized filoplumes or UV-scattering nanostructures in skin (not full avian plumage), unless lineage is explicitly ex-avian founder from F27; keep stamina benefit on ridges, visibility cost in meadows.
fixes: Call it patagial and dorsal keratinized filoplumes or UV-scattering nanostructures in skin (not full avian plumage), unless lineage is explicitly ex-avian founder from F27; keep stamina benefit on ridges, visibility cost in meadows.

analogues.organism: Budgerigar and blue tits: structural coloration in feather barbs manipulates UV reflectance; analogous UV scatter in butterfly wings (Morpho).

chains.trait: Hooked talons locking into bark immovable in wind
links: Wind force per m/s is 1.6× Earth's; gales push light creatures
Gliders need stable perching to avoid being blown away
Hooks evolve to grip uneven rock and bark
Allows resting and hunting from fixed vantage points

skill.effect: Attaches to cliff or tree; immune to wind and push effects; can ambush from above.

chains.weakness: Cannot move while perched; slow to detach if attacked.
observe: Claws dig into rock or bark; creature immovable in strong wind.
Head turns while body remains fixed.
Gale howls, but creature sleeps on spire.

journal.en: The gale screams; the creature sleeps.

plausibility.summary: F19 (1.6× wind force per m/s) favours low-profile gripping and heavy claw purchase on dyke rock and giant-tree bark (F21). Gliders that sleep on spires need static perches; trade-off (immobile while locked) is realistic.
fixes: F19 (1.6× wind force per m/s) favours low-profile gripping and heavy claw purchase on dyke rock and giant-tree bark (F21). Gliders that sleep on spires need static perches; trade-off (immobile while locked) is realistic.

chains.trait: Curved beak snatching fruit mid-air from Rondo herds
links: East meadows have fruit abundance; Rondo herds love fruit
Competition for fruit drives niche specialization
Alula evolves aerial raiding to avoid ground competition
Beak shape optimized for tearing fruit and small prey

skill.effect: Snatches fruit from Rondo or Zanco herds; interrupts their eating; +15% intimidation.

chains.weakness: Rondo spits can hit glider; Garfio may raid Alula's cache.
observe: Alula dives, snatches fruit from Rondo's mouth, and rises.
Rondo herds panic and spit at the sky.
Alula caches stolen fruit in moss.

journal.en: It steals fruit from the herd with a laugh in its wings.

plausibility.summary: Steal from low branches, moss caches, or fruit Rondo holds at browse height during pauses; use glide-dive + short flap burst (Engage) rather than chase; Rondo spit weakness stays.
fixes: Steal from low branches, moss caches, or fruit Rondo holds at browse height during pauses; use glide-dive + short flap burst (Engage) rather than chase; Rondo spit weakness stays.

relations.note: (council kind 'Predator/Thief') Garfio raids nests; Alula steals from Garfio's mouth using speed. Garfio finds Alula too fast to catch consistently.
(council kind 'Competitor') Alula steals fruit from Rondo herds; Rondo cannot reach. Rondo herds view Alula as a nuisance.

moments: Silhouetted against the evening star, an Alula drops from the rock spire, snatches a Rondo's fruit mid-air, and vanishes into the mist before the herd can spit.

journal.en: The wind holds it up. It steals fruit from the herd with a laugh in its wings.
It sees the world from the spire; a secret of height.
